note: The envelope itself (BRIDGE.md §2). A malformed message gets a response too: a bad message must not leave a promise pending forever in the page, which is why every case here has one — including the ones where `id` could not be read and comes back as the empty string.

cases.name: an unknown method
cases.note: Unreachable in a matched pair — the injected shim defines only the methods the shell registered — so this is what a plugin calling the handler directly gets (SPEC §6.1: plugins are full-trust and can).

cases.note: The reverse mismatch — bundle newer than shell — is refused here; bundle older than shell degrades in the page instead (BRIDGE.md §8).
